subject: Order Form: payment flow, currency responsibility & next steps for legal redlines
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@veridian.ai>, Procurement Ops <procure@veridian.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Order Form: payment flow, currency responsibility & next steps for legal redlines

Hi Maria / Procurement team —

Thanks for sending the redline earlier today. I pulled together a short list of commercial items we should align on so finance and legal can close the Order Form quickly:

- Payment routing & currency: Veridian indicated payments will originate from your EU entity, but the Order Form currently lists USD billing to the US entity. Can you confirm which legal entity will invoice and which currency you want on the Order Form? This affects tax/VAT treatment and the payment instructions in Section 4.
- Net terms and acceptance of electronic invoices: Redwood typically does Net 30 for self-serve accounts; for enterprise we can agree Net 45 on a quarterly invoicing cadence. Please confirm whether Net 45 is acceptable. Also confirm acceptance of emailed PDFs vs. portal-only invoices.
- Minimum commit schedule: your team proposed a ramp (Q2: 25%, Q3: 50%, Q4: 100%). Finance asked whether we can move to calendar-month proration rather than quarter blocks — this reduces unused committed spend.
- Taxes & VAT: need clarity on VAT responsibility and a copy of your VAT registration (if EU entity). If Veridian is VAT-registered in the EU and paying from the EU entity, we can zero-rate VAT on our invoice with the proper evidence.

I've attached our redline (OrderForm_Redline_v2.docx) with inline comments for finance/legal. If you can confirm entity + currency and whether Net 45 works, our legal team will integrate the responses into a clean order form and get it back for signature.

Can we aim to close this by EOD Thu so we can hit the customer onboarding window?

Thanks —
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0112

Attachment: Veridian_OrderForm_Redline_v2.docx (docx)
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@veridian.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Ops <procure@veridian.ai>, contracts@veridian.ai
Date: 2027-04-11T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form: payment flow, currency responsibility & next steps for legal redlines

Hi Rachel —

Thanks for the summary. Quick answers below, and I've looped in our legal/finance contacts.

- Entity & currency: Payments will originate from Veridian AI B.V. (NL entity). We prefer EUR on the order form.
- Net terms: Net 45 is acceptable for this deal.
- Minimum commit schedule: We can accept calendar-month proration instead of quarter buckets — that should work better for our internal forecasts.
- VAT evidence: attaching our VAT certificate and PO (see PO_4578.pdf).

We are redlining a couple of clauses in the MSA re: data residency and audit logs; our counsel will send a single consolidated redline later today. In the meantime, please update billing entity & currency and the payment instructions to show Veridian AI B.V. / EUR.

Regards,
Maria Gomez
Head of Legal Operations | Veridian AI
maria.gomez@veridian.ai

Attachments: Veridian_PO_4578.pdf (pdf)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-12T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Order Form: payment flow, currency responsibility & next steps for legal redlines

Rachel — forwarding Maria's note. From a finance/legal ops perspective, a few items for our redline pass: 

1) Update Section 4 billing entity to Redwood's standard language for third‑country invoicing when customer entity != Redwood contracting entity. Laura, can you drop in the clause that handles cross-border VAT responsibility and the invoicing party? We should also add an explicit line that payments in EUR will be converted per the exchange rate on invoice date if Redwood invoices in USD for any reason.
2) PO filing: Finance needs the PO number on the face of the invoice (Veridian PO 4578).
3) Net terms: confirm Net 45 in the Order Form and add late-fee waiver for the first 30 days to smooth the pilot.
4) Proration: accept calendar-month proration language; add an example in a new Schedule A so both sides run the same calculation.

If Laura can push a clean Order Form with these edits I can pre-clear with Finance and then we send to Maria's counsel. Target: Laura, can you get a draft back by EOD 4/12?

- Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@veridian.ai>
Cc: Procurement Ops <procure@veridian.ai>
Date: 2027-04-14T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form: payment flow, currency responsibility & next steps for legal redlines

Hi all —

Attached is a clean Order Form that implements the items Ben flagged: updated billing entity (Veridian AI B.V.), currency = EUR, Net 45, PO number on invoice, calendar-month proration example in Schedule A, and a short VAT clause that says Veridian is responsible to provide valid VAT evidence and Redwood will zero-rate the invoice if evidence is provided. I also added the late-fee waiver for the first 30 days as a commercial concession for the pilot.

We left the MSA data-residency redlines for separate counsel discussion; that doesn't block Order Form signature. Maria — please confirm your counsel is OK with the updated billing instructions and the VAT mechanic; if so, we'll issue via DocuSign and coordinate signatories.

I've attached the clean Order Form + redline comparison.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
